entities.name: (S)-lactic acid
entities.definition: An optically active form of lactic acid having (S)-configuration.

entities.name: calcium carbonate
entities.definition: A calcium salt with formula CCaO<small><sub>3</sub></small>.

entities.name: <small>D</small>-glucose 6-phosphate
entities.definition: A <small>D</small>-glucose monophosphate in which the phosphate group is attached to position 6.

entities.name: acetaldehyde
entities.definition: The aldehyde formed from acetic acid by reduction of the carboxy group. It is the most abundant carcinogen in tobacco smoke.

entities.name: acetone
entities.definition: A methyl ketone that consists of propane bearing an oxo group at C2.

entities.name: pyruvate
entities.definition: A 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of pyruvic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

entities.name: acetic acid
entities.definition: A simple monocarboxylic acid containing two carbons.

entities.name: water
entities.definition: An oxygen hydride consisting of an oxygen atom that is covalently bonded to two hydrogen atoms

entities.name: (−)-menthol
entities.definition: A p-menthan-3-ol which has (1R,2S,5R)-stereochemistry. It is the most common naturally occurring enantiomer.

entities.name: ATP
entities.definition: An adenosine 5'-phosphate in which the 5'-phosphate is a triphosphate group. It is involved in the transportation of chemical energy during metabolic pathways.

entities.name: glycine
entities.definition: The simplest (and the only achiral) proteinogenic amino acid, with a hydrogen atom as its side chain.

entities.name: (S)-malate(2−)
entities.definition: An optically active form of malate having (S)-configuration.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-tartaric acid
entities.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of tartaric acid.

entities.name: formate
entities.definition: A monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of formic acid. Induces severe metabolic acidosis and ocular injury in human subjects.

entities.name: hexadecanoic acid
entities.definition: A straight-chain, sixteen-carbon, saturated long-chain fatty acid.

entities.name: <small>D</small>-fructose
entities.definition: Fructose is a levorotatory monosaccharide and an isomer of glucose.  Although fructose is a hexose (6 carbon sugar), it generally exists as a 5-member hemiketal ring (a furanose).

entities.name: NAD<small><sup>+</small></sup>
entities.definition: The oxidised form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide found in all living cells. In metabolism, NAD<small><sup>+</small></sup> is involved in redox reactions, carrying electrons from one reaction to another.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-glutamic acid
entities.definition: An optically active form of glutamic acid having <small>L</small>-configuration.

entities.name: adenosine 5'-monophosphate
entities.definition: A purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate having adenine as the nucleobase.

entities.name: cholesterol
entities.definition: A cholestanoid consisting of cholestane having a double bond at the 5,6-position as well as a 3β-hydroxy group.

entities.name: ammonia
entities.definition: An azane that consists of a single nitrogen atom covelently bonded to three hydrogen atoms.

entities.name: benzoate
entities.definition: The simplest member of the class of  benzoates that is the conjugate base of benzoic acid, comprising a benzoic acid core with a proton missing to give a charge of -1.

entities.name: methane
entities.definition: A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is attached by single bonds to four hydrogen atoms. It is a colourless, odourless, non-toxic but flammable gas (b.p. −161°C).

entities.name: oleic acid
entities.definition: An octadec-9-enoic acid in which the double bond at C-9 has Z (cis) stereochemistry.

entities.name: urea
entities.definition: A carbonyl group with two C-bound amine groups. The commercially available fertilizer has an analysis of 46-0-0 (N-P2O5-K2O).

entities.name: ethanol
entities.definition: A primary alcohol that is ethane in which one of the hydrogens is substituted by a hydroxy group.

entities.name: hydrogen peroxide
entities.definition: An inorganic peroxide consisting of two hydroxy groups joined by a covalent oxygen-oxygen single bond.

entities.name: carbon dioxide
entities.definition: A one-carbon compound with formula CO<small><sub>2</sub></small> in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food.

entities.name: (S)-lactate
entities.definition: An optically active form of lactate having (S)-configuration.

entities.name: ADP
entities.definition: A purine ribonucleoside 5'-diphosphate having adenine as the nucleobase.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-tryptophan
entities.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of tryptophan.

entities.name: NADH
entities.definition: A coenzyme found in all living cells; consists of two nucleotides joined through their 5'-phosphate groups, with one nucleotide containing an adenine base and the other containing nicotinamide.

entities.name: citrate(3−)
entities.definition: A tricarboxylic acid trianion, obtained by deprotonation of the three carboxy groups of citric acid.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-alanine
entities.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of alanine.

entities.name: oxalic acid
entities.definition: An α,ω-dicarboxylic acid that is ethane substituted by carboxyl groups at positions 1 and 2.

entities.name: xylitol
entities.definition: A pentitol (five-carbon sugar alcohol) having meso-configuration, being derived from xylose by reduction of the carbonyl group.

entities.name: carbon monoxide
entities.definition: A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is joined only to a single oxygen. It is a colourless, odourless, tasteless, toxic gas.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-phenylalanine
entities.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of phenylalanine.

entities.name: maltose
entities.definition: A glycosylglucose consisting of two <small>D</small>-glucopyranose units connected by an α-(1→4)-linkage.

entities.name: hydrogencarbonate
entities.definition: The carbon oxoanion resulting from the removal of a proton from carbonic acid.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-cysteine
entities.definition: An optically active form of cysteine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

entities.name: <small>D</small>-glucose
entities.definition: A glucose with <small>D</small>-configuration.

entities.name: lactose
entities.definition: A glycosylglucose disaccharide, found most notably in milk, that consists of <small>D</small>-galactose and <small>D</small>-glucose fragments bonded through a β-1→4 glycosidic linkage. The glucose fragment can be in either the α- or β-pyranose form, whereas the galactose fragment can only have the β-pyranose form.

entities.name: glycerol
entities.definition: A triol with a structure of propane substituted at positions 1, 2 and 3 by hydroxy groups.

entities.name: propan-2-ol
entities.definition: A secondary alcohol that is propane in which one of the hydrogens attached to the central carbon is substituted by a hydroxy group.

entities.name: hydrogen chloride
entities.definition: A mononuclear parent hydride consisting of covalently bonded hydrogen and chlorine atoms.

entities.name: <small>D</small>-glucitol
entities.definition: The <small>D</small>-enantiomer of glucitol (also known as <small>D</small>-sorbitol).

entities.name: sucrose
entities.definition: A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.

entities.name: dinitrogen
entities.definition: An elemental molecule consisting of two trivalently-bonded nitrogen atoms.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-lysine
entities.definition: An <small>L</small>-α-amino acid; the <small>L</small>-isomer of lysine.

entities.name: (1→4)-β-<small>D</small>-glucan
entities.definition: A β-<small>D</small>-glucan in which the glucose units are connected by (1→4) linkages.

entities.name: dihydrogen
entities.definition: An elemental molecule consisting of two hydrogens joined by a single bond.

entities.name: vanillin
entities.definition: A member of the class of benzaldehydes carrying methoxy and hydroxy substituents at positions 3 and 4 respectively.

entities.name: phosphate(3−)
entities.definition: A phosphate ion that is the conjugate base of hydrogenphosphate.

entities.name: nicotine
entities.definition: A racemate composed of equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-nicotine.

entities.name: sodium chloride
entities.definition: An inorganic chloride salt having sodium(1+) as the counterion.

entities.name: sulfuric acid
entities.definition: A sulfur oxoacid that consists of two oxo and two hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central sulfur atom.

entities.name: caffeine
entities.definition: A trimethylxanthine in which the three methyl groups are located at positions 1, 3, and 7. A purine alkaloid that occurs naturally in tea and coffee.

entities.name: ethyl acetate
entities.definition: The acetate ester formed between acetic acid and ethanol.

entities.name: starch
entities.definition: The most important reserve polysaccharide found in plants. It is a glucan consisting of amylose and amylopectin.

entities.name: amylopectin
entities.definition: A polydisperse highly branched polysaccharide derivative composed of chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage. The chains are joined together by α(1→6) glycosidic linkages. A small number of α(1→3) glycosidic linkages and some 6-phosphate ester groups also may occur. The branches in amylopectin typically contain 24 to 30 glucose residues.

entities.name: glycogen
entities.definition: A polydisperse, highly branched glucan composed of chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage, joined together by α(1→6) glycosidic linkages. A small number of α(1→3) glycosidic linkages and some cumulative α(1→6) links also may occur. The branches in glycogen typically contain 8 to 12 glucose residues.

entities.name: amylose
entities.definition: A glucan composed of unbranched chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage. The number of repeated glucose subunits (n) is usually in the range of 300 to 3000, but can be many thousands. One of the two components of starch (the other, 70-80%, being amylopectin). Cf. linear maltodextrin, in which the chain length is typically between 3 and 17 glucose units.

entities.name: ammonium
entities.definition: An onium cation obtained by protonation of ammonia.

entities.name: theobromine
entities.definition: A dimethylxanthine having the two methyl groups located at positions 3 and 7. A purine alkaloid derived from the cacao plant, it is found in chocolate, as well as in a number of other foods, and is a vasodilator, diuretic and heart stimulator.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-ascorbic acid
entities.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of ascorbic acid and conjugate acid of <small>L</small>-ascorbate.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-glutamate(1−)
entities.definition: An α-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of <small>L</small>-glutamic acid, having anionic carboxy groups and a cationic amino group

entities.name: acetate
entities.definition: A monocarboxylic acid anion resulting from the removal of a proton from the carboxy group of acetic acid.

entities.name: ATP(4−)
entities.definition: A nucleoside triphosphate(4−) obtained by global deprotonation of the triphosphate OH groups of ATP; major species present at pH 7.3.

entities.name: oxalate(2−)
entities.definition: A dicarboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of oxalic acid.

entities.name: benzoic acid
entities.definition: A compound comprising a benzene ring core carrying a carboxylic acid substituent.

entities.name: formic acid
entities.definition: The simplest carboxylic acid, containing a single carbon. Occurs naturally in various sources including the venom of bee and ant stings, and is a useful organic synthetic reagent. Principally used as a preservative and antibacterial agent in livestock feed. Induces severe metabolic acidosis and ocular injury in human subjects.

entities.name: citric acid
entities.definition: A tricarboxylic acid that is propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 2. It is an important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms.

entities.name: (S)-malic acid
entities.definition: An optically active form of malic acid having (S)-configuration.

entities.name: potassium chloride
entities.definition: A metal chloride salt with a K(+) counterion.

entities.name: pyruvic acid
entities.definition: A 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid that is the 2-keto derivative of propionic acid. It is a metabolite obtained during glycolysis.

entities.name: citrate(2−)
entities.definition: A tricarboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of two of the three carboxy groups of citric acid.

entities.name: <small>L</small>-ascorbate
entities.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of ascorbate and conjugate base of <small>L</small>-ascorbic acid, arising from selective deprotonation of the 3-hydroxy group. Required for a range of essential metabolic reactions in all animals and plants.
